messages.content: my neighbor brought me some cake on a plate. i have washed the plate, but i have not returned it yet. i want to thank her without turning it into a long visit.
you could take the plate back and say a short thank you at the door. do you want to ask before coming over, or do you already know a good time?
i do not know when she will be home. i can send a message first.
then you could write: thank you for the cake. i have your clean plate ready to return. when would be a good time to bring it over?
she says this afternoon, but i have to leave for work soon after lunch.
you can tell her when you are free and ask whether that works. for example: i can come by just after lunch, before i leave for work. would that be okay?
i do not want her to think i am asking for more cake.
your message is about returning the plate and saying thank you. you can keep it there without asking what she has made today.
what if she asks me to come in?
you can thank her and say you have to leave for work soon. if you want to visit another day, you can say that too, but you do not need to choose a day before you know your time.
write what i could say at the door.
thank you again for the cake. i have to go to work soon, so i cannot stay today. it was kind of you to bring it over.
my daughter wrote a little story on three pages. the pages got out of order. she wants me to help without choosing the order for her.
you could ask her what happens at the start, then help her find the page with that part. after that, ask what happens next. she can choose the order while you help keep the question clear.
the story starts with a girl leaving home. another page has her coming back. the last page in our hand has her at a market.

then you have three parts to ask about: leaving home, being at the market, and coming back. you can ask whether she goes to the market before coming home, or whether something different happens in her story.
she says the girl goes to the market, comes home, then speaks to her father about it.
then the order she wants is leaving home, going to the market, and coming back to tell her father. you can put the pages in that order if each page has one of those parts.
what if one page has both the market and coming home?
then the parts do not each need a whole page. read the start and end of each page with her, and ask which sentence should come next.
i want her to know i am listening rather than making a different story.
you could say: this is your story. i am helping you find the order you want. tell me which part comes first, and we can read from there.
i am waiting at the hospital with my cousin. i keep asking if they are okay, and they keep saying yes. i do not know what else to say.
you could ask whether they would like to talk or would rather have some quiet. being there can be help even when you do not have many words to say.
i am not asking about what is wrong or how to help with that. i just want to sit with them in a kind way.
then keep it simple and let your cousin choose. you could say: i am here with you. would you like to talk about something, or shall we just sit for a while?
they say they want to talk about something else, not the hospital.
you could ask about something they enjoy, such as a book, a meal, or music. choose a question that gives them room to answer without having to talk about why they are there.
they have been reading a book. i do not know what it is about.
you can ask: what is the book you are reading about? if they want to tell you, you can listen and ask about a part they bring up.
what if they stop talking after a short answer?
you do not need to keep talking through every quiet moment. you can sit with them and let the conversation rest. if you are not sure, ask whether they would like more quiet.
write one short question about that.
would you like to keep talking, or would you rather sit quietly for a little while?
i was going to walk with my friend, but now there is rain. i still want to see them. i do not want my message to sound like i want to stop the whole plan.
you can say you still want to meet and ask about doing something inside. that keeps the visit clear while changing the part about walking outside.
we could meet at my house and make tea. can you write that?
i still want to see you today. with the rain, would you like to come to my house for tea instead of going for a walk?
i do not know if they like tea.
then leave the drink open or ask what they would like. you could say: would you like to come to my house instead? we could have something to drink and talk.
they say they would rather walk even in the rain. i do not want to.
you can say that clearly without saying their choice is wrong. you could write: i would like to see you, but i do not want to walk in the rain today. would meeting inside work for you?
what if it does not?
then you may need a different day or a different plan that works for both of you. you can want to meet without having to choose the same thing every time.
make a question about another day.
would you like to choose another day for our walk?
i went to a shop and did not see the rice i wanted on the shelf. can i say the shop has no rice?
you can say you did not see that rice on the shelf. there might be more in another part of the shop, so asking a worker would give you more information.
what should i ask if i mean that specific type?
you could say: do you have more of this type of rice, or is this all there is today? if you have a picture or an old container, you can show it to make clear which type you mean.
i have an old container. i do not want to buy a different type without knowing.
then show the container and ask whether they have that one. if they ask whether you want another type, you can ask what is different before choosing.
what if the worker says they do not know?

then you know that person has not given you a clear answer. you can ask whether another worker could help, or choose to look another time. you should not turn an answer that is not clear into a fact about what the shop has.
write a short conversation with the worker saying they can ask someone else.
do you have this type of rice? i am not sure, but i can ask another worker. thank you, i would like that.
what did that conversation tell me about the rice?
it told you someone would ask. it did not yet tell you whether the rice is there.
a song makes me think of my grandmother. my brother heard the same song and said it did not make him think of her. i thought it might.
people can hear the same song and remember different things. did you hear it with your grandmother at a time your brother was not there?
yes. she played it when i visited after school. my brother was at work then.
then you have a specific memory with the song that he may not have. that can explain why it brings your grandmother to mind for you without doing the same for him.
i want to tell him about it rather than say he should feel the same.
you could say: she used to play this when i visited after school. that is why it makes me think of her. i know you were usually at work then.
he asked what we did while it played. we made food together.
then you could add that detail. it gives him a picture of the time you remember: we listened to the song while we made food together.
should i say what food we made if i do not remember?
if you do not remember, you can keep the food general. the part you know is that you listened to the song while you made food together.
can i ask whether he has a different memory of her?
yes. you could ask: is there something that makes you think of her in that way?
my friend asked what i think of a drawing. i like the trees, but i do not understand what is happening in the middle. i want to be kind and clear.
you can say what you like and ask about the part you do not understand. for example: i like the trees near the side. could you tell me what is happening in the middle?
is asking better than saying the middle is wrong?
if you do not understand the meaning yet, a question can help you learn what your friend wanted to show. not understanding a part is different from knowing it is wrong.
they say the people in the middle are waiting for a train. i thought they were inside a house.
now you can explain what you saw without choosing a change for them. you could say: i first thought they were inside a house. now that you say they are waiting for a train, i understand the idea.
i want to ask if they want help making that clear.
you could ask: would you like to talk about how to make the station clear in the picture, or did you only want to know what i saw?
why give them that choice?
because asking what you think is not always asking you to change the drawing. your friend may want to hear your first thought before choosing what to do next.
make the question shorter.
would you like ideas, or do you just want to hear what i saw?
picoboi, make this shorter for a message i will send: i am going to be late because i left my book at home and had to go back for it.
i will be late because i went back home for my book.
why did you write i when you are not the person going back home?
you asked for a message that you will send. i kept i so the message speaks from your place when you use it. i am not saying i went home myself.
how would you say it outside the message?
the message is for you to send as your own words. outside that message, i should say you went back home for your book.
now tell me what happened using you.
you left your book at home, went back for it, and will be late.
make the message a question asking whether my friend can wait.
i had to go back home for my book and will be late. could you wait for me?
does the question mean the friend has said yes?
no. it asks for their answer. they may say yes, no, or ask how long you will be.
i think i will be ten minutes late, but i am not sure. add that without making it sound known.
i had to go back home for my book. i think i will be about ten minutes late. could you wait for me?
